issues.description: Using 'var' instead of 'const' or 'let' for variable declaration. 'var' has function scope and can lead to unexpected behavior.
issues.suggestion: Replace 'var results = []' with 'const results = []' since the array reference doesn't need reassignment.

issues.description: Using 'var' in loop declaration. 'var' is function-scoped and can cause closure issues.
issues.suggestion: Replace 'var i = 0' with 'let i = 0' for proper block scoping.

issues.description: Using 'var' for loop variable inside the loop body.
issues.suggestion: Replace 'var t = todos[i]' with 'const t = todos[i]' since it's not reassigned.

issues.description: No null/undefined check on 't.title' before calling toLowerCase(). Will throw TypeError if title is null or undefined.
issues.suggestion: Add safety check: 'if (t && t.title && t.title.toLowerCase().indexOf(query.toLowerCase()) !== -1)' or use optional chaining: 't.title?.toLowerCase()'

issues.description: Using loose equality (==) instead of strict equality (===). Can lead to unexpected type coercion.
Using loose equality (==) instead of strict equality (===).
Using loose equality (==) instead of strict equality (===).
Using 'var' instead of modern variable declaration.
issues.suggestion: Replace 'var sorted = results' with 'let sorted = results' or create a copy with 'const sorted = [...results]' to avoid mutating the original.

issues.description: Direct assignment without cloning. The sort() method mutates the original array, affecting the 'results' parameter.
issues.suggestion: Clone the array first: 'const sorted = [...results]' before sorting to avoid side effects.

issues.description: Using traditional for-loop instead of more modern and readable array methods.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: 'return todos.filter(t => t.title?.toLowerCase().includes(query.toLowerCase()))' for better readability and performance.

issues.description: query.toLowerCase() is called on every iteration. Should be computed once.
issues.suggestion: Move 'const lowerQuery = query.toLowerCase()' outside the loop and reuse it.

issues.description: RegExp constructor with user input without escaping. Vulnerable to RegExp Denial of Service (ReDoS) and can cause exceptions with special regex characters.
issues.suggestion: Escape special regex characters: 'const escapedQuery = query.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, "\\$&"); const re = new RegExp(escapedQuery, "gi");'

issues.description: Returning raw HTML with <mark> tags. This could lead to XSS if the title contains user-generated content with HTML/script tags.
issues.suggestion: HTML-escape the title before adding markup, or return structured data instead of HTML strings. Consider: escaping title first, then wrapping matches, or using a safe templating approach.

issues.description: No validation on Date parsing. Invalid dates will result in NaN comparisons.
issues.suggestion: Add date validation: 'const dateA = new Date(a.createdAt); const dateB = new Date(b.createdAt); if (isNaN(dateA) || isNaN(dateB)) return 0; return dateA - dateB;'

issues.description: No validation of input parameters. Function doesn't handle null/undefined/empty inputs gracefully.
issues.suggestion: Add input validation at the start: 'if (!todos || !Array.isArray(todos)) return []; if (!query || typeof query !== "string") query = "";'

issues.description: Manual string comparison for sorting is verbose.
issues.suggestion: Use localeCompare for string sorting: 'sorted.sort((a, b) => a.title.localeCompare(b.title))' for proper internationalization support.

codeQuality.summary: This file has critical security vulnerabilities in the highlightMatch function (XSS and ReDoS risks) and multiple bug-risk issues including loose equality comparisons, missing null checks, and array mutation. The code uses outdated JavaScript patterns (var, traditional loops) affecting maintainability. Immediate attention needed for security issues before production use.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Empty or whitespace-only queries could return all todos or cause unexpected behavior. This is a common user input scenario that should be handled explicitly.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test searchTodos(todos, '') and searchTodos(todos, '   ') to verify expected behavior (return empty array or all todos)

untestedPaths.reasoning: Passing null or undefined as query will cause a runtime error when calling .toLowerCase(). This would crash the application.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test searchTodos(todos, null) and searchTodos(todos, undefined) - should handle gracefully or throw descriptive error

untestedPaths.location: searchTodos() - todos with missing title property
untestedPaths.reasoning: If a todo object lacks a 'title' property, accessing t.title.toLowerCase() will throw 'Cannot read property toLowerCase of undefined', causing a crash.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test searchTodos([{completed: true}], 'test') to verify error handling for malformed todo objects

untestedPaths.reasoning: Should safely return empty array, but needs verification to ensure loop doesn't cause issues.
Attempting to access .length on null/undefined will throw 'Cannot read property length of null/undefined', crashing the application.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test searchTodos(null, 'query') and searchTodos(undefined, 'query') - should handle gracefully

untestedPaths.reasoning: If status is anything other than 'all', 'active', or 'done', the function falls through to return todos unchanged. This implicit behavior should be tested or made explicit.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test filterByStatus(todos, 'invalid') and filterByStatus(todos, null) to verify fallback behavior

untestedPaths.reasoning: Filter functions check t.completed, which could be undefined for malformed todos, leading to unexpected filtering results.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test filterByStatus([{title: 'test'}], 'active') to verify handling of todos missing completed property

untestedPaths.reasoning: If sortBy is neither 'title' nor 'date', results are returned unsorted. This implicit no-op should be tested.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test sortResults(results, 'invalid') and sortResults(results, null) to verify no sorting occurs

untestedPaths.location: sortResults() - todos missing createdAt for date sort
untestedPaths.reasoning: When sortBy is 'date', accessing a.createdAt or b.createdAt on todos without this property will result in 'Invalid Date' comparisons, producing unpredictable sort order.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test sortResults([{title: 'a'}, {title: 'b'}], 'date') to verify handling of missing createdAt

untestedPaths.location: sortResults() - invalid date strings in createdAt
untestedPaths.reasoning: new Date() with invalid date strings returns Invalid Date, which can cause NaN in subtraction, leading to incorrect sort order.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test sortResults([{createdAt: 'invalid'}, {createdAt: '2024-01-01'}], 'date') to verify sort stability

untestedPaths.reasoning: Array.sort() mutates the original array. Since 'sorted' is assigned as 'results' (not a copy), this mutates the input parameter, which could cause unexpected side effects.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test that sortResults() does not mutate the original input array, or document this as expected behavior

untestedPaths.location: highlightMatch() - special regex characters in query
untestedPaths.reasoning: If query contains regex special characters like '.', '*', '(', '[', etc., new RegExp(query, 'gi') will throw a SyntaxError or produce incorrect matches.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test highlightMatch('test (item)', '(item)') to verify proper escaping of regex special characters

untestedPaths.reasoning: Passing null or undefined to new RegExp() will convert to string 'null'/'undefined' and create a valid but incorrect regex pattern.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test highlightMatch('title', null) and highlightMatch('title', undefined) to verify error handling

untestedPaths.reasoning: Empty query creates a regex that matches every position, potentially wrapping every character in <mark> tags or causing unexpected output.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test highlightMatch('test', '') to verify expected behavior with empty query

untestedPaths.reasoning: The search() function chains all other functions but has no standalone tests visible. Edge cases from component functions could compound.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test search() with various combinations: empty query, null status, invalid sortBy, empty todos array

testCoverage.summary: This file has no visible test coverage and contains multiple critical vulnerabilities including null/undefined parameter handling, missing property access crashes, and regex injection risks. The searchTodos() and highlightMatch() functions are particularly dangerous as they will crash on null inputs or special characters. Additionally, sortResults() mutates its input array, which could cause bugs in calling code.

refactorings.summary: This file extensively uses outdated ES5 patterns including var declarations, function expressions, indexOf, and verbose comparison logic. Modernizing to ES6+ with const/let, arrow functions, includes(), localeCompare(), and strategic use of filter/map will significantly improve readability, reduce bugs from scope issues and type coercion, and make the code more maintainable. The current implementation also lacks input validation and has a potential RegExp injection vulnerability in highlightMatch.
